Myzyakiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Mizyakiv's Jewish community numbered 178 people (8 percent) in 1887, supported by a synagogue from 1889; the population reached 307 (15.7 percent) by 1897. Jews were engaged in trade and crafting; Rabbi Meileh Derbarimdiker served the community in 1905, and by 1914 Jews owned the town's drugstore, its only mill, two timber yards, and seven grocery shops. Following the July 1941 occupation, all of Mizyakiv's Jews were executed that August. This cemetery, established per the Commission on the Preservation of Jewish Heritage in the early 19th century, reportedly still held visible gravestones as late as the 1970s, according to local testimony, before being demolished to make way for a collective farm; part of the land remains under private agricultural share today, though its owner is no longer actively involved in managing the site, and locals remain certain of the cemetery's former location despite the lack of physical traces.
